properties.name: Clay-rich delta top
properties.why: Sample clay-bearing rock on top of the delta, where clay minerals point to rock that sat in water.
properties.photo_caption: Example from Jezero: rock slabs at "Jigging Cove", where Perseverance searched for clay-bearing rocks.
properties.geology: Flat, firm ground on the delta top (slope 3°, thermal inertia 354, so consolidated rock rather than sand). CRISM D2300 (Fe/Mg clay) passes our threshold in 58% of cells within 50 m and in every cell within 25 m: the strongest clay patch in the square.
properties.position_source: Chosen 14 Nov from our real layers: CRISM minerals.png, THEMIS thermal_inertia.tif and the HiRISE hazard map (green cell). Lat/lon planetocentric, from the site grid (data/grid.py).

properties.name: Delta front scarp
properties.why: Read and sample the layers exposed where the delta front drops toward the crater floor.
properties.photo_caption: Example from Jezero: Kodiak, a butte of layered rock left from the river delta.
properties.geology: Edge of the delta front: the ground falls about 30 m within 50 m, with slopes up to 25° nearby (stay on the green ledge; red cells within 50 m). Thermal inertia 344, among the rockiest on the site, so bedrock is exposed here. CRISM shows no strong mineral signal at this spot.
properties.position_source: Chosen 14 Nov from our real layers: CRISM minerals.png, THEMIS thermal_inertia.tif and the HiRISE hazard map (green cell). Lat/lon planetocentric, from the site grid (data/grid.py).

properties.name: Olivine-rich crater floor
properties.why: Sample olivine-rich rock on the crater floor, the rock that turns into carbonate when it reacts with carbon-dioxide-rich water.
properties.geology: Flat crater floor south of the delta (slope 4°, elevation range 4 m within 50 m). CRISM OLINDEX3 (olivine) passes in 18% of cells within 50 m, the strongest olivine patch away from the site edge. Carbonate (MIN2295_2480) passes in only 13 scattered cells in the whole square, so no carbonate stop is supported by our data.
properties.position_source: Chosen 14 Nov from our real layers: CRISM minerals.png, THEMIS thermal_inertia.tif and the HiRISE hazard map (green cell). Lat/lon planetocentric, from the site grid (data/grid.py).
